text: Hypertrophy can be achieved across a wide spectrum of loading zones, with no differences apparent at the whole-muscle level. Low-load training emphasizes metabolic stress and promotes the greatest increases in local muscular endurance, whereas low-repetition, high-load training requires high levels of mechanical tension and enhances the ability to lift heavier loads as a result of greater neural adaptations. Some evidence suggests there may be a fiber type-specific response in which heavy-load training produces greater cross-sectional area increases in Type II fibers, and light loads have a preferential effect on Type I hypertrophy.
